verdict.rationale: Secureframe documents a Custom Integrations capability for creating and mapping custom resources from tools it has no native integration with. Raw data can be pushed via an API endpoint, and Secureframe then normalizes, maps, and tests it. This is backed by a published REST API reference with an embedded OpenAPI 3.0 spec and a versioning policy. Missing for 10: no independent or hands-on corroboration that custom pushes work as claimed, and no explicit documentation of pushing pre-computed test results or evidence artifacts (only raw resource data that Secureframe tests itself).

support.subject: As a developer, I can build private/custom integrations against a documented API to push evidence and test results from systems the catalog doesn't cover

citations.quote: Custom Integrations, which enables you to create and map custom resources from tools and services that Secureframe doesn't offer a native integration with.
Push raw data via an API endpoint or CSV upload and let Secureframe handle normalization, mapping, and testing for compliance-related resources
Ingest data from cloud, on-prem, hybrid, or legacy systems and even custom-built tools.
Secureframe exposes a REST API for use by customers, partners, and community developers.
the document embeds the full "openapi: 3.0.0 / info: title: Secureframe API" OpenAPI definition
